#1974. Steve McManaman says he ‘feels sorry’ for two Arsenal stars

Steve McManaman said he ‘felt sorry’ for Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz following Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta’s playing style means the forwards often ‘get the blame’ for the side’s more cautious performances.

Arsenal maintained their unbeaten record in this season’s Champions League as a pair of first-half strikes from Noni Madueke and Gyokeres proved decisive before Wiktor Nowak’s late consolation.

The result ensured the Gunners, last year’s runners-up, sit third four matches into their league-phase campaign following previous victories over Napoli and Lille and a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

September’s 3-0 defeat at the hands of Brighton in the Premier League remains Arsenal’s only loss in all competitions this term, an impressive run that Arteta’s men will look to continue when they return to action at home to Hull this weekend.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta made a total of six changes to his team that got the better of Liverpool on Sunday, with Gyokeres starting through the middle in place of Havertz at Prague’s Fortuna Arena.

The Sweden international has endured a tough start to the new season but played a key role in the opening goal, assisting Madueke with a hooked pass behind Slavia Prague’s defence for Arsenal’s breakthrough inside just nine minutes.

He then got on the scoresheet himself to double the visitors’ advantage shortly before the break, beating Nazar Domchak with a superb effort that went in off the upright.

While it proved a far more difficult second half for Gyokeres as Arsenal held firm to protect their lead, ex-Liverpool and Real Madrid star McManaman felt the striker should have come away proud with his night’s work.

However, the ex-England international expects Havertz to return to Arteta’s starting XI when the north Londoners return to top-flight action against Hull on Saturday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I liked him in the first half. I think in the second half, when Arsenal became a little bit dishevelled, they weren’t as close to him so I think it’s hard,’ McManaman said of Gyokeres’ performance.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘When they are playing well, he is up there on his own. In the first half, they were very compact, they were very close to him, they were getting around the sides, they were making chances, so he looked dangerous.

‘In the second half, when it got really stretched and they were wide and he was up on his own, he looked as if he was just left alone a lot.

‘I think when Arsenal play as more of a unit, attacking and defending together, I think he looks better.’

Given Arsenal aren’t renowned for being the most ‘entertaining’ of teams, McManaman finds himself ‘feeling sorry’ for Gyokeres and Havertz in certain matches.

‘I do feel sorry for Arsenal forwards sometimes because they’re not an entertaining team, they’re not like a Barcelona. They defend very deep, they defend as a whole and it’s a long way to get to the other end of the pitch to score goals,’ he added.

‘They’re never going to be this entertaining, lovely, free-flowing side scoring goal after goal after goal, and then Gyokeres and Havertz sometimes get the blame because of that. It’s normally the midfielders and the defenders that we talk about.

‘But as I said, Gyokeres had a great first half, he did his best in the second half and he deserves what he got because he got an assist and he got a goal.’

Asked if it could be time for Arteta to trust Gyokeres with more minutes, McManaman replied: ‘Whenever a big game comes around, Arteta reverts to Havertz doesn’t he?

‘People keep saying that Havertz scores goals in the big games and he certainly did that against Liverpool so you can’t really contest that.

‘But I just think he trusts Havertz a little bit more. That’s all it is.

‘Gyokeres played against Slavia Prague and he did exactly what he needed to do. He had an impact on the game, he had a huge impact on the game and we’ll wait and see for Saturday.

‘But I always think that when big games come around, if it was a final or Arsenal or Manchester City, if both Gyokeres and Havertz are fit, then Arteta would always revert back to Havertz.’

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Arteta heaped praise on Gyokeres’ all-round display, applauding the Swede’s ‘connection’ with his team-mates.

The Arsenal head coach explained: ‘I thought he was really good. It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

‘He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.’

On Gyokeres’ combination play, Arteta added: ‘He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

‘So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.’

Asked whether not starting had been a challenge for Gyokeres, Arteta replied: ‘It’s a question for him, but I’d imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different.

‘The players need to impact the game like he has done today when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It’s really positive for the team.’

#1973. Austin FC vs Portland Timbers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 08:59

Austin FC host Portland Timbers in a Major League Soccer Decision Day fixture at Q2 Stadium on Saturday.

A win would clinch a playoff place for Portland, while Austin, already eliminated, play the last match of Davy Arnaud’s interim spell before Jim Curtin takes over.

Austin FC sit 14th in the Western Conference and were eliminated from playoff contention by consecutive defeats to Real Salt Lake on October 28 and LA Galaxy on October 31.

Arnaud has been in charge on an interim basis since Nico Estevez was dismissed on May 18, and Curtin, the former Philadelphia Union head coach, takes over on December 1 or at the end of the season, whichever is later.

The Galaxy defeat was settled early, with Joao Klauss scoring in the 10th minute, Hirving Lozano in the 38th and Robert Taylor in the 48th to leave Austin three goals down before the hour.

Ervin Torres pulled one back in the 54th minute with a long-range strike for his second career MLS goal, set up by Micah Burton - who was making his first MLS start - and Jorge Alastuey, before Sergi Roberto made it 4-1 in the 66th minute.

Damian Las made two saves in the 35th minute to keep the score at 2-0 at that stage, and Riley Thomas came off the bench to make his MLS debut.

On a brighter note, Austin have scored in each of their last seven matches, having last been held scoreless by FC Dallas on September 20.

Myrto Uzuni and Christian Ramirez both have nine goals and would reach double figures with a goal on Saturday.

Austin also won the last meeting 2-1 at Providence Park on August 29, with Facundo Torres scoring the opener and Oleksandr Svatok netting the winner in stoppage time.

Portland Timbers are eighth in the West on 43 points, with 12 wins, seven draws and 14 defeats from their 33 matches, and a run of three straight victories has lifted them into a wild-card position.

Marti Cifuentes’s side were in a seven-game winless run between early September and mid-October, so a third successive playoff appearance in his first season would mark a sharp turnaround.

The three wins came against Charlotte FC, St. Louis City and Houston Dynamo, all of whom are heading to the post-season, and the Timbers scored nine goals across those fixtures.

The 3-1 victory over Houston on November 1 featured a 18-8 shot advantage, with six efforts on target compared with one for the visitors.

Vincent Janssen, a mid-season signing, scored his fifth goal of the season against Houston and added two assists, the first of his MLS career.

Kristoffer Velde scored his 11th goal of the season in the same game, and American Soccer Analysis rated him the most valuable outfield player in MLS outside Lionel Messi since the World Cup break.

David Da Costa scored the opener and took his team-leading assist tally to 11 from the corner that Janssen headed in for the third.

The Timbers rank ninth in MLS for goals scored but 22nd for goals conceded, and they have kept only two clean sheets this season.

A win clinches a playoff place and keeps seventh spot and a round-one berth, within reach, while a draw only secures qualification with help from other results.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:

Austin will do without Chris Applewhite (quad) and Jon Bell (lower abdomen) for Matchday 34, while Zan Kolmanic is suspended following his red card against LA Galaxy.

Uzuni and Ramirez are both available to chase double figures, and Facundo Torres, scorer of the August opener in Portland, is also available.

Portland have six players listed as out: Alex Bonetig (shoulder), Brandon Bye (knee), Jimer Fory (concussion), Zac McGraw (back), Juan Mosquera (foot/ankle) and goalkeeper Trey Muse (concussion).

Janssen, Velde, Da Costa and Ariel Lassiter are all available again.

Las; Desler, Sanchez, Biro; Burton, Sabovic, E. Torres, Alastuey; Placheta, Gallagher, Ramirez

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:

Pantemis; Hernandez, Surman, Waterman, Smith; Izoita, Caicedo, Da Costa; Lassiter, Velde, Janssen

Portland arrive with the clearer motivation and the stronger recent evidence, as nine goals in three wins against playoff-bound opponents sit alongside a front line in which Janssen, Velde and Da Costa are all producing.

Austin conceded three goals inside 48 minutes at the Galaxy, are heading for a bottom-two finish in the West, and have nothing to play for beyond individual milestones and the chance to give their academy players further minutes.

The Timbers have not lost in Austin since 2021, and their need for a result should decide a game in which both sides score.

#1972. Mikel Arteta reveals reaction to Noni Madueke's England snub as Arsenal get boost

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has backed Arsenal winger Noni Madueke to recover quickly from his latest England disappointment.

Madueke was not named in Thomas Tuchel’s Three Lions squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

That is despite the 24-year-old putting together the best run of form in his Arsenal career so far, stepping up in the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka.

Madueke has four goal involvements in his last eight matches and sent Arsenal on their way to victory over Slavia Prague in the Champions League in midweek by opening the scoring.

It has been a timely run, with Saka out with a quad injury, and it came after Madueke was also omitted from the England squad for the last international window in September.

Arteta revealed at the time that Madueke had been the best player in training after that setback, and the Arsenal boss was again full of praise on Friday as he expanded on how the winger has cemented his place in the Gunners’ side.

“What he did was go abroad and he trained,” Arteta said. “He got somebody to train and he wanted a programme. He wanted to do that. That’s Noni and that’s his mindset. He wants to get better.

“I love that action that he took because in that moment he wasn’t playing. When he’s playing and everybody’s talking about you, it’s easy to do.

“When he was in a difficult moment that time, what he did helped him to after start being in the team and make the impact that he made. I’m very happy with him.”

Tuchel said it was a “close call and a difficult decision” to leave Madueke out of his latest England squad.

Rio Ngumoha, Josh King and Morgan Gibbs-White were among those preferred in forward areas to the 24-year-old.

“That was an option for Thomas,” Arteta said. “There were so many options, he needs to make decisions. He made that one this time. That’s it. I leave it completely to him.”

Dave Challinor has done plenty of talking in his first week as Sheffield Wednesday manager, and when the action starts at Boundary Park on Sunday evening, the message to his new players is clear.

The 51-year-old has had his first week on the Middlewood Road training pitches, and now he is anxious to see how his new players put it into practice in the FA Cup first round at Oldham Athletic.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I'm really looking forward to it, more as my first real eyes on from a dugout position," said the former Colwyn Bay, Fylde, Hartlepool United and Stockport County manager.

"There will be information we've given the players and we want to see how they can carry those things out.

"We know between now and Christmas the run of games we have got of Saturday-Tuesdays and we go against some of the sides you would expect to compete for promotion.

"We have to hit the ground running. We've got to continue to develop whilst winning.

"The players I won't say have been bombarded. We have to prioritise the bits that are important.

"There are things that have been in place that are good and we have to make sure we continue to improve on those things but just add bits.

"It won't be immediate change, it'll be constant over the next couple of weeks.

"We have done quite a bit without going into too much detail. I hope you will see in the first game the changes that we want to look at.

"We've got a really good group of players and we need to try to facilitate their best bits on a football pitch, regardless of the opposition. That's what we'll try and do."

Challinor's job is to try and learn about his squad.

"I will speak to all the players," he said. "Everyone has different drivers, different markers.

"But if you can't enjoy being a footballer at Sheffield Wednesday, especially when you're at home in front of 30,000 people – I'd worry for you.

"Will there be some mistakes? Of course there will. But I'm really intrigued to see what they've got from the start from a pitchside, from a dugout perspective.

"I've got true belief that we'll produce a performance befitting of everything that happens on Sunday in terms of the travelling supporters."

He needs professional pride to be a factor in the 5.15pm TNT Sports game at League Two Oldham.

"They're a little bit up and down in terms of results," said Challinor. "They had a good result on Tuesday going to Northampton and winning.

"It's the FA Cup. From our side of things I don't imagine playing on a Sunday at 5.15 would have been the case if they'd have thought it was a synch and a walkover.

"We've got to go and be Sheffield Wednesday, that's the most important thing for us.

"We've got really good players, they need to perform for ourselves and for the supporters – undoubtedly we'll have a full away end – and show what we're about.

"There's been things said about the team recently that aren't nice. Use that as a motivation."

Di’Shon Bernard is available having has trained all week, but the bulk of the Owls' injured players will not be back until next week's league game at home to Plymouth Argyle, which now looks set to go ahead. Liam Cooper, Joe Lumley and Ali Al-Hamadi could feature then.

"They're probably not too far away in terms of being back in training to a certain degree," said Challinor.

"We've got the midweek fixture against Accrington (in the EFL Trophy). We have to plan. It's not something you'd ideally do in November, but that's where we are."

For now, that might mean players having to play out of position.

"That's probably going to be the case for the next few weeks," warns Challinor.

"You would love to put people into positions where they are comfortable but that's not always the case that you can do it.

"There's been plenty of adversity over the course of the season with injuries, suspensions and all them things and that continues because we've still got players out but we can't use that as an excuse.

"We hope over the next couple of weeks it will get better because we'll get numbers back which will allow us more options as players back from injury and I would expect that we'll get stronger and stronger."

Sil Swinkels is suspended after his red card against Blackpool.

Will Grainger will miss next week's games after being selected by Wales for their European Under-19s Championship qualifiers against Finland, Spain and Iceland.

Sunday's game will be played to a finish, with extra time and penalties to decide who goes into Monday's draw.

#1970. Sky Germany: Krösche heading for Milan but compensation must be discussed – the situation

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Now, Sky Germany confirm that Krösche’s future likely lies in Italy because a move to Milan is becoming increasingly likely. However, no deal has been finalised yet: officials from both clubs still need to hold talks as Krösche is only on leave from Frankfurt.

His contract, which runs until 2028, is currently still valid. The 46-year-old insisted on having a release clause included in his contract. Specifically, this means that any club wanting to hire him before the summer of 2027 will have to pay a fee of approximately €5-7m, or negotiate with Eintracht.

No advanced talks have yet taken place, but Sky do add that Krösche is expected to take on the role of Head of Football with Milan. A start date of January 1, 2027 – coinciding with the start of the winter transfer window – is being discussed.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

#1969. Bukayo Saka ‘a bit fragile,’ reckons former Arsenal and Manchester United defender

Bukayo Saka is ‘a bit fragile’ and must work on preventing injury problems in future, reckons former Arsenal defender Mikael Silvestre.

The Gunners winger is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem picked up in a Champions League clash with Bayern Munich on October 21.

Saka is not expected to be back in action until December, with Noni Madueke filling in on the right flank in his absence.

The 25-year-old has been hampered by some injury issues over the last two seasons, but has still managed to rack up a huge amount of appearances, 323 for Arsenal in total.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He played 49 times in all competitions last season, although the 2024/25 campaign saw him play the least since he broke into the first team, turning out 37 times.

Silvestre accepts that injuries are bound to occur for players of Saka’s ilk, but suggests he is not quite as robust as he could be.

‘When you are an explosive player like Saka, obviously the muscles are what will trouble you when you are doing those sprints all the time,’ Silvestre told PariuriX.com. ‘Maybe, he is a bit fragile, and with the amount of games things like this can happen.

‘What is important for him is the recovery and the prevention, because it’s very important for him that it doesn’t happen too often, because he is very important for Arsenal.’

Silvestre sees Madueke as an improving force in Saka’s absence, although there is still room to become sharper in the final third.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘That’s why you have a big squad and Madueke would start for most of the teams in the Premier League, if not all,’ said the Frenchman. ‘He has the quality and I think he is getting his confidence now, he is trying to score and create more.

‘He doesn’t have the killer instinct yet, but he is growing into it and he is trying to get there.’

Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with Manchester United, reckons Arsenal’s forward line as a whole can let them down, with their strength clearly lying in defence. The recent 1-0 win at Liverpool being a good illustration.

‘Winning at Anfield, with a clean sheet as well makes it a very good defensive performance,’ he said. ‘We can’t say the same with the offense. I would say that’s one for the record, and one that you look back at the end of the season and say it was an important 3 points. But it wasn’t a full on, top class, 90 minute performance from Arsenal.

‘But it’s important to get those wins against teams who are also potentially in the race, and to keep your distance from them.

‘The positives are the defensive side of things, the 3 points, and the fact that it was at Anfield. It breaks that negative dynamic but I think it’s just for the stats really.

‘I think you need your best players at the key moments featuring in the semi-finals and the final of competitions. Arsenal need to keep Timber fit, Saliba is coming back also. You need your strong 11 and the best defence once you reach the final. So it’s still a long way away but they defend well, as a unit for sure.’

The Blues head to the Stadium of Light hoping to build on last Saturday’s 2-0 win over 10-man Manchester United at Stamford Bridge.

Young goalkeeper Mike Penders kept a clean sheet in that game as summer signing Martinez continued his recovery from surgery following the fractured jaw he suffered in last month’s victory against Everton.

But Martinez - wearing a protective face mask - was this week involved in Chelsea training at Cobham and could play on Wearside, depending on whether Xabi Alonso is keen to immediately reinstate his No1. Martinez’s recovery has been ahead of schedule and he could feature.

Moises Caicedo was not spotted during the 15 minutes of Wednesday’s training session that was open to the media, and Alonso has said it is due to discomfort he felt after the United match. The final training session before the trip to Sunderland, on Saturday, will also be used as a guideline for Caicedo’s availability.

Previously injured Argentine defender Aaron Anselmino has also been involved in training, after being selected to play for his country over the upcoming international window.

Romeo Lavia started in Jordan Henderson’s place against United and excelled so could keep his spot in midfield, with the latter having missed out through illness.

Estevao started against United and impressed so is another player who Alonso may find it difficult to bench.

Joao Pedro and Maxence Lacroix are both still sidelined, along with Jorrel Hato and captain Reece James, who is recovering from knee surgery and unlikely to be available again until January.

Winger Jamie Gittens suffered an ankle injury on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month. He will be out for “a few weeks”, Alonso said a fortnight ago.

#1967. ‘Ridiculous threat’ – Xabi Alonso told that ex-Liverpool star would ‘thrive’ at Chelsea

Alan Hutton believes that Trent Alexander-Arnold would ‘thrive’ if he reunited with former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

Alexander-Arnold left his boyhood club Liverpool to join the Spanish giants two summers ago, but injuries saw him feature just 21 times in the league under Alonso and his interim replacement, Alvaro Arbeloa.

While fit this campaign, the Englishman has still struggled for regular minutes under Jose Mourinho and has started just one of Real’s last six matches in all competitions.

Summer signing Denzel Dumfries has moved above Alexander-Arnold in the pecking order, while Mourinho has also deployed Federico Valverde as a makeshift right-back over the Englishman.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Given that lack of game time, Hutton believes that Alexander-Arnold may soon start to consider his options.

And the former Premier League full-back earmarked Chelsea as the perfect club to get the 28-year-old back to his best.

‘Trent Alexander-Arnold could thrive at Chelsea because Xabi Alonso would use him in the correct manner and get the best out of him, because his attacking threat is ridiculous,’ Hutton told OLBG.

‘What he sees, his vision, his passing ability, it’s right up there.

‘It is strange when you watch Real Madrid, I was watching El Clásico and Valverde played at right-back while Dumfries and Trent were on the bench.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Even for me, as good a player as Valverde is, he’s a midfielder, so that would hurt you a bit. It’s been a shame that it hasn’t quite worked out, but he’s so talented.

‘I think a move back to the Premier League would suit him, he knows it inside out. Someone like Alonso, with what he’d want from him, would use him in the correct manner and get the best out of him.’

Speaking recently, Mourinho admitted that omitting Alexander-Arnold has been a painful decision.

‘First of all, it hurts me. I don’t like to make players feel bad. I want them to feel good,’ Mourinho said.

‘Obviously, when you build a squad with two players per position as your foundation and then have a third player take the field, that’s something I don’t like.

‘But there are things that are more important than these feelings. Things that are more important for the team at a given moment. And I decided that right now, the move was to change up the midfield and put Fede [Valverde] in there.’

And with speculation likely to mount ahead of the January transfer window, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield.

‘I’d have him back,’ Carragher said on The Overlap. ‘He would get a lot of criticism, because I think he made a mistake. I think he made a big mistake going to Madrid.

‘We’ve definitely missed his creativity.’

#1966. FC Cincinnati vs Nashville SC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 01:11, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:06

FC Cincinnati will look to secure a spot in the first round of the MLS playoffs when they take on Nashville SC at TQL Stadium on Saturday.

Nashville head into MLS Decision Day with their fate already sealed, having clinched their first-ever Supporters' Shield.

Cincinnati are sitting in seventh spot in the Eastern Conference after winning 12, losing 11 and drawing 10 of their 33 matches this season.

Pat Noonan's side have come into form at just the right time, having dropped just two points from their last four matches since suffering consecutive defeats against New England Revolution and Columbus Crew.

Cincinnati recorded home and away wins in back-to-back games against DC United, before they played out a thrilling 2-2 draw against Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Orange and Blue then returned to winning ways with a narrow 1-0 home victory against Philadelphia Union, which came courtesy of Ayoub Jabbari's third goal of the season.

Having already guaranteed some form of post-season action, Cincinnati will secure a spot in the first round with a win against Nashville, but a failure to claim all three points will leave them open to being overtaken by Columbus and Orlando City, who currently occupy the two wild-card round positions.

The hosts can take some confidence from the fact they have won two of their last three MLS home games against Nashville, including a 2-1 success in September 2025 at TQL Stadium.

Nashville will already have one eye on the first round of the playoffs after clinching their first MLS Supporters' Shield with a 2-0 win over Montreal last month.

BJ Callaghan's side went on to play out a goalless draw against Philadelphia Union before coming from two goals down to pull off a 3-2 victory over New York Red Bulls last time out.

Sam Surridge netted a stoppage-time winner in that comeback success, which extended the club's impressive 17-game unbeaten home run in the MLS.

In fact, they have gone nine matches without defeat at any venue since losing away to Toronto FC on September 27, so they will be desperate to carry that undefeated streak into the playoffs as they continue to work towards their ultimate goal of winning the MLS Cup for the first time in their history.

Having tied the MLS single-season points record, Nashville will take the outright record if they are able to add at least a point to their 74-point tally in their final outing of the regular season.

Nashville will certainly fancy their chances of claiming a positive result after running out 4-0 winners in their most recent meeting with Cincinnati at Geodis Park in August.

Cincinnati defender Tyrell Malacia is unlikely to prove his fitness in time, having been forced to sit out the last three matches with an ankle injury.

The hosts are also without the services of Julian Malatini and Miles Robinson, while Teenage Hadebe is hoping to prove his fitness after being withdrawn with an apparent injury issue in the win over Philadelphia.

Evander is in contention to start the final regular season game after featuring as a half-time substitute last weekend.

As for the visitors, they have reported no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday's away trip, which should give Callaghan a full squad to choose from.

The likes of Daniel Lovitz, Edvard Tagseth, Alex Muyl and Warren Madrigal could come into Callaghan's thinking if he wants to manage minutes ahead of the playoffs.

That said, Surridge will surely be keen to retain his place as he looks to add to the 19 goals he has scored in the regular season.

Schwake; Najar, Palacios, Woledzi, Lovitz; Espinoza, Yazbek, Tagseth, Muyl; Madrigal, Surridge

Nashville carry a nine-game unbeaten run into Saturday's fixture, and while there may be changes to their starting lineup, we think they will do enough to extend their undefeated streak with a draw.

#1965. Arsenal v Hull City: Sergej Jakirovic's plans A, B and C to avoid another nightmare against Europe's elite

His Tigers take on Arsenal side who he regards as one of the two best teams in Europe on their own patch in Saturday's Premier League.

He has come up against Europe’s elite before, and found out the hard way how tough it can be.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Jakirovic was coach of Dinamo Zagreb when they faced Bayern Munich in the 2024-25 Champions League group stage and was on the wrong end of a 9-2 defeat which saw him sacked two days later.

At the time it was the biggest victory in Champions League history, although Como outdid that with Tuesday's 9-1 win at Lens.

"Especially this night, we were not at this level at all, and if you are not compact, if you are shuffling, especially when they try to play around you to pull you out of your position, they will use all these gaps between your players, because they recognise this immediately," said Jakirovic.

"In that game they had three penalties (all scored by Harry Kane), which is a little bit weird, but they will use every mistake, they will punish you, they will not miss their opportunities.

"We tried something this week. We tried everything – plan A, plan B, even C.

"But you don't have a chance if you sit back like 5-4-1 and if you are passive, they will destroy you.

"It has to be front foot, it has to be aggressive on the body especially because they have a very high quality in their roster.

"You can be more solid, more aggressive, especially in the challenge, especially the second goal against Ipswich (in last week's 2-1 defeat). We could stop this easily, we can make a foul at least. At this level, it's a goal.

"Arsenal are playing very good football, no matter Champions League or Premier League. They are very strong, they control everything not just against us, also other better clubs.

"Obviously, they are a big favourite, and we can start to try to create some difficulties for them."

Fortunately, Hull have already shown this season and last they are made of tough stuff if they concd arly.

"You need to be really mentally strong if this happens," said the former Bosnia player.

"Every goal is very important, especially for the goal difference, and also we have to show mentality like we always do.

"We already had this experience – Chelsea away game, Newcastle away – but we should try to avoid this 100 per cent.

"Our mental resilience is very important because of everything we did in the past – this team, together, chemistry, togetherness, team spirit, everything. So this is the main thing we have."

Asked what he would talk to Mikel Arteta about if he shares a drink with the Gunners manager at full-time, Jakirovic replied: "I will ask him to give me his budget!

"But he deserves to be at this level. He was (a coach) at Man City, now he's been at Arsenal (as manager) almost seven years, and it's progress every year.

"It's not easy to build a new team, but you have options to add more quality in your team, because Arsenal is a top-five team in Europe, in terms of everything.

"This a chance to show we can compete there. Maybe you can surprise them with something, and also you can compare where we are right now, because they are the best, it's not a secret."

Ryan Gravenberch is Liverpool’s only injury concern ahead of the Premier League clash against Crystal Palace.

The Dutchman, who was dropped for last weekend’s 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal, missed the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce due to a heel injury that prevented him from travelling to Istanbul.

Gravenberch’s availability at the weekend remains up in the air with Andoni Iraola revealing the midfielder is in a race against the clock to prove his fitness ahead of the trip to Selhurst Park.

Alisson Becker is under some scrutiny over his performance after the defeat by Fenerbahce, following on from his mistake against Arsenal.

Alexander Isak’s impressive scoring streak may have ended against Arsenal, but the Swede bagged a seventh goal in 13 appearances with his maiden Champions League strike of the season against Fenerbahce.

#1962. The Man Utd change Michael Carrick must make against Aston Villa to keep his job

With JJ Gabriel almost out the door at Old Trafford Manchester United, and Michael Carrick will now be tempted to pin all their hopes on another emerging star in Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old has played himself into first-team contention after a dazzling display off the bench in Tuesday’s comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

While it was Bruno Fernandes’ penalty that sparked the revival and Matheus Cunha’s brace that got them over the line, Lacey’s fearless cameo on the right was the catalyst for change.

Even the perennially reserved Michael Carrick couldn’t hide his delight over the performance, noting the teenager has ‘that bit of mischief’ in his locker that troubled Roma for the final 15 minutes of the game. Lacey ended the contest playing in defence after Cunha’s red card with Carrick jokingly christening him his new right-back.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Lacey’s sharp, perfectly-weighted passing enabled United to get up the pitch with real intent – seldom seen this season. He completed every one of his attempted passes and completed all but one of his duels. Operating in tight spaces just in front of the touchline, his first touches and clever exchanges were on point from the moment he came on. His pass for Cunha’s winner couldn’t have been placed better.

It has been a long time coming for Lacey. Injuries shelved tentative plans for him to make his debut at 16 under Erik ten Hag in 2023 and it was a tough road back from those issues that threatened to halt his progress.

‘Everybody in the world knows about Shea Lacey,’ United’s former Under-21 manager Travis Binnion said last year. ‘So he needs a little bit of fortune, he needs to be patient with himself and everybody else needs to be really patient with him.’ That patience could now be about to pay off.

Whether Tuesday’s win was a turning point or another false dawn for United remains to be seen. Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer led United to delirium-inducing comeback victories over Newcastle United in Atalanta with identical scorelines when the pressure was mounting on their shoulders. Both were gone shortly after.

But with Carrick’s back against the wall, there is the opportunity to roll the dice with Lacey. The Liverpool-born talent thumped home a wonderful strike in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton but has seen just 31 minutes of action off the bench since. Excluding the second-half performance against Roma, United’s attack has lacked any verve or real invention. A change is needed and Lacey will feel this is his chance.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It was on the right where he caused damage midweek with Amad Diallo making way for him after 75 minutes. It had been another disappointing evening for the Ivory Coast international who spurned huge opportunities against Chelsea four days earlier.

Since forcing his way back into the side under Erik ten Hag, Amad has been looked upon as United’s most naturally talented winger. But his goal and assist return has fallen woefully short of expectations. He is now approaching one year without a goal, last finding the back of the net in the 4-4 draw with Bournemouth on 15 December. In that time, he has provided two assists – one on the final day of last season against Brighton and the other for Joshua Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 4-1 humiliation in Como two weeks ago.

His haul of 14 goals during his magnificent campaign with Sunderland in the 2022-23 season is a distant memory. A hat-trick against Southampton in January 2025 helped him to an impressive haul of 11 goals and 10 assists in his first full campaign back in Manchester but seven goal involvements in 40 appearances since the start of the 2025-26 campaign is not good enough.

Wayne Rooney alluded to Amad’s problem midweek and made his case for Lacey getting the nod.

‘Amad does some really good things, but it’s that end product, that is what takes you to the next level,’ he told Amazon Prime. ‘And the glimpses of what I’ve seen from Lacey when he has come on…he has got something in there, that little touch and little pass which United needed to get them over the line in this game.’

The win over Roma has shifted a few clouds amid the gloom hanging over Old Trafford and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa now looks a more inviting environment for Carrick to make the change and put his faith in Lacey.

#1961. Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur: Daniel Farke on 'elite' duo on opposing sides at Elland Road

Something else sets them apart from their contemporaries.

It was brought into sharp focus by Harry Kane's recent elevation to Ballon d'Or winner amid a glittering ceremony in his home city of London.

Kane's staggering goalscoring numbers and consistency speaks for itself, but it hardly happened overnight.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

What sets him apart is his elite mentality from an early age. 'Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise' was his social media post after being named as the best footballer in the world.

For all his trappings and status, no one could ever describe him as narcissistic.

That message might just resonate with two players on opposing sides today: Archie Gray and James Trafford.

The former, of course, is well known to Leeds United supporters. In an ideal world, he will still be stepping out in the white of Leeds and not Tottenham Hotspur.

It's hard to believe that Gray is still not yet 21 - that milestone arrives in March.

He is part-way through his third season in the Premier League and fourth campaign as a first-teamer. He is not far shy of 150 competitive games already in a career which is surely only going one way.

Capable of playing centre-back, full-back and midfield, he is a manager's dream. Tactically adept, responsible and mature beyond his years, it's easy to see that he belongs to a revered football dynasty.

He is also driven, football-obsessed and low-maintenance. The sort of person - and not just player - that Daniel Farke likes. Even if he will not be wanting to see any of his acumen today.

Farke said: "It was early to see (his elite mentality). When Archie came through at the age of 17, he replaced my vice-captain and our club legend Luke Ayling.

"It was not an easy decision. It was not for the dressing room. I came in as the new coach and I've got a club legend. Together with Liam Cooper, he was wearing the captain's armband.

"But he was on the bench because I played Archie, a 17-year-old kid. But Archie had already at this age more or less this mentality and the quality. He was a different drawer (top-drawer).

"The same when I played him in midfield - you had experienced players like Glen Kamara, for example, out for his position. But just due to the quality and mentality that (Gray) he had meant he was ready and prepared to play on a Championship level.

"I think he has also sometimes worn the captain's armband for Tottenham at a more prominent level.

"It says a lot about him and you need this quality and mentality if you want to be there as a young player playing so many games on this level."

As with Kane, Gray has had to handle knockbacks - being part of a Spurs side that has flirted with relegation in the past few seasons. It's something that Leeds and England goalkeeper Trafford also knows a fair bit about.

The 24-year-old heads into the game on the back of a howler in last weekend's loss to Bournemouth - gifting a goal to Cherries player Evanilson.

He was also culpable—though by no means as damningly - for Riccardo Calafiori's goal in United's 2-1 reverse at Arsenal on October 10.

Mistakes are - and will forever remain - an omnipresent part of a goalkeeper's life.

Trafford also currently has the best save percentage in the Premier League at 80.5. Only Hull City's Konstantinos Tzolakis - with 32 saves - has stopped more shots so far this term.

So the Cumbrian, from a humble farming roots near Cockermouth, has plenty to shout about if he cares to. Which he doesn't.

Farke said: "He's really top. James has delivered top performances for us so far.

"He was, of course, involved in the first goal (at Bournemouth) and sadly in this case it was then decisive, but that's also what you have to deal with, especially as a young player and young goalkeeper.

"You deal with these setbacks and learn from them and it's quite important for me that he didn't look shy of confidence during this week.

"He was there with his normal performance. I'm pretty sure he has also learned from it, but for me it's also important that he doesn't lose his confidence and his rhythm. Of course, he will be in goal and also hopefully with an important display."

Speaking of statistics, Leeds head into the game in receipt of an unwanted Premier League record: they have not won a top-flight game played before 3pm on a Saturday in 21 attempts since March 2022.

Ending that statistic would be a nice way to head into an international break, not that Farke is losing any sleep over it.

"I wouldn't take too much into the timing', the German opined.

"I think it's also normal. In the last years we were on Premier League level, we've spent more or less all the time in the relegation pattern, so it's less likely to win games in comparison to Man City or Liverpool or Arsenal right now. It's another chance to break the record, it's important to be switched on."

#1960. Mansfield Town vs Macclesfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:46, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:16

Arriving at One Call Stadium as underdogs, famous giant killers Macclesfield will face League One's Mansfield Town in the FA Cup's first round proper.

The Stags have only been eliminated at this stage in one of the last seven seasons, though the Silkmen are in strong form, despite their lower-division status.

Nigel Clough's Mansfield enjoyed their run to the FA Cup's fifth round in 2025-26, and they will be confident of kicking off their campaign in strong fashion this weekend.

That being said, the Stags have endured a mixed season so far, and head into this clash having won two, drawn two and lost one of their last five games.

Most recently, Clough's side were held to a 0-0 draw by relegation-threatened Wigan Athletic on Tuesday, marking the second consecutive match in which they have failed to score, following a 2-0 defeat to Notts County.

Those blanks have left Mansfield sitting 11th in League One with 19 points from 13 games, though a push for promotion is far from impossible, considering they are just three points behind sixth-placed Reading.

A run in the FA Cup could serve as a morale boost for a playoff charge, and supporters will be expecting to see the Stags progress at One Call Stadium, where they have lost just one of their six league outings this term.

Meanwhile, John Rooney's Macclesfield are best known for knocking out then-holders Crystal Palace in the FA Cup's third round last term, but they will need to navigate a pair of tough tests to make it through to face another Premier League club this time around.

This may be the first round proper, but the National League North side have already beaten Redcar Athletic 2-1, Scarborough 2-1 and Anstey Nomads 3-0 to reach this stage.

Those hard-fought victories have only served to bolster the Silkmen's resolve to prove they are more than a mere novelty, and having downed Bedford 3-0 last weekend - their fourth win in six games - the club will be cautiously optimistic.

That latest success marked a second clean sheet in three matches for Rooney's men, who boast the joint-best defensive record in the sixth tier, having conceded just 11 goals in 13 fixtures.

Macclesfield are also pushing for promotion in the National League North, where they are third with 27 points, a tally that has them just two off top-of-the-table South Shields.

However, the visitors remain significant underdogs, even if they have only tasted defeat once on the road across all competitions this season, winning six times and drawing twice.

Mansfield will be without centre-back Baily Cargill once again due to a hamstring injury, while Kyle Knoyle was forced off against Wigan through injury.

In their absence, Luke Bolton could start alongside Adedeji Oshilaja and Ryan Sweeney in the Stags' defence, flanked by Nathan Moriah-Welsh and Jordan Bowery.

Further forward, Michael Smith and Rhys Oates could lead the attack, platformed by a midfield featuring Louis Reed, George Maris and Elliott Hewitt.

As for Macclesfield, they are missing left-back Brandon Lee as he recovers from a long-term leg injury that has kept him sidelined since last season's FA Cup second round win over Slough in December 2025.

On Saturday, Cameron Borthwick-Jackson could operate on the left of a four-man defence, next to Tom Wilson, Sam Heathcote and Ammar Dyer.

Mansfield may have blanked in their last two matches, but they should have enough to get over the line against a sixth-tier opponent.

Macclesfield are one of the strongest sides in the National League North and could put up a fight, yet it would still come as a surprise to see anything other than a home win on Saturday.

#1955. Arsenal handed new William Saliba boost after France squad announcement

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have been handed a welcome boost over William Saliba after Zinedine Zidane named his second France squad.

Former Real Madrid head coach Zidane is preparing to take charge of Les Bleus for just the fifth time after replacing Didier Deschamps, who stood down following the 2026 World Cup in north America earlier this summer.

The first post-World Cup international window was an extended one which lasted three weeks with France facing Belgium twice, Italy and Turkey in a Nations League quadruple-header.

France took four points from a possible 12 to sit top of League A, Group 1 ahead of facing Italy and Turkey within the next nine days.

Zidane’s first France squad did not contain Saliba as the Arsenal defender was still recovering from a back injury sustained while playing for the national team in the World Cup semi-final against eventual winners Spain.

Saliba has since resumed full fitness. He played 45 minutes for the Gunners in a behind-closed-doors friendly last week before travelling with the squad to the Czech Republic for the 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

However, the 25-year-old has not been selected by Zidane for France duty this month.

The news will be welcomed by Mikel Arteta as Saliba should benefit from more time in training, though the Frenchman will miss out on some valuable minutes to build up his match sharpness.

“We’ve been in very close contact,” Arteta said on Friday ahead of Arsenal’s Premier League clash against Hull. “They’re announcing [their squad] at 5pm this evening.

“They have all the information, now it’s about them, about Zinedine in this case to make the call. We will accept whatever it is.”

After the international break, Arsenal face Newcastle at St James’ Park, with home games to follow against Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City.

#1954. Liverpool injury, suspension list and return dates for Crystal Palace: Ryan Gravenberch, Hugo Ekitike latest

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:58

Liverpool will look to respond to their latest defeat by beating Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds not only lost 1-0 against Arsenal in the Premier League last weekend, but they also lost 3-2 against Fenerbahce on Wednesday in the Champions League.

Andoni Iraola cannot afford to head into the next international break on the back of a third consecutive loss in all competitions.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace.

Possible return date: November 8 (vs. Crystal Palace)

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, and he has cast doubt on whether the Dutchman will be involved before the international break, though he has not ruled him out of featuring in some capacity against Palace.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

The right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him."

Possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City)

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some time, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The plan was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one]."

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

#1950. Former Man Utd chairman slams owners after controversial Avram Glazer comments

Former Manchester United chairman Martin Edwards expects supporters to be furious with Avram Glazer’s comments on the club and has accused the owners of getting their priorities wrong.

The Athletic report that Glazer made a controversial point while speaking to financiers at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London in September.

One of the owners of the Red Devils compared Manchester United to the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys as a brand that will remain commercially successful irrespective of how well they are performing on the pitch.

Edwards, who was chairman of Manchester United from 1980-2003, expects fans to react badly to that sentiment and has encouraged the current owners to train all their focus on improving the team.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘I heard that this morning and I thought “By Jove, what’s the reaction going to be from the supporters?” Supporters don’t want to hear that!’ Edwards said on talkSPORT.

‘Supporters want to hear that you’re winning trophies. They’re not interested in profits or dividends or what people are taking out of the club. They want the club to be successful, they want the best players, they’d rather be spending money on the team than on the new stadium.’

Edwards accepts that running a club the size of Manchester United is a tricky business and owners must satisfy various stakeholders, but he feels the balance is currently off.

‘When I was running United, I always felt I had three responsibilities, really,’ he said. ‘One: in those days we were still developing the ground, so I had to build the ground and develop the ground. Look after the team, which is always the most important. But also, because we were public we had to pay dividends and keep the shareholders happy.

‘It’s a balance. Running a football club is a complete balance, from top to balance. It’s a question of whether you get it right or wrong.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He added: ‘I think it’s quite clear, in my eyes, that the team is the most important element at the moment. You’ve got to get the team right and forget new stadiums if you’re not going to fill them. Get the team winning again and get the supporters behind you. We’re not a united front at the moment.’

The landscape of top flight football has changed considerably since Edwards was in charge at Manchester United and he believes it has not all been for the better.

‘You’ve got owners now who don’t attend games. They put somebody in charge, whatever else,’ he said. ‘Existing owners now, they wouldn’t know who’s in the team.

‘It’s become big business and what you can get out of it. The game has changed and for the older ones of us it’s disappointing, really, the direction it’s gone.’

Looking back to the start of Manchester United’s decline as a title-challenging force in the Premier League, Edwards suggests it was the loss of Alex Ferguson and CEO David Gill in 2013 and Ed Woodward being named as Gill’s replacement.

‘Once Alec and David Gill decided to leave in 2013, that was a huge blow to the club and they’ve never really recovered from that,’ he said.

‘If you wanted to be critical you’d say right from the beginning when they replaced David Gill, they replaced him with not a football man, but a merchant banker.

‘If you’ve got the top of the football chain who’s not converse with football, that does make it difficult. I think that once the mistakes start, they multiply.

‘Recruitment has been a big problem. Look at the players they’ve bought, some of them haven’t been up to the standard. Generally it snowballs. That’s been the problem.

‘Also, have United spent enough money to be able to compete at the top? Manchester City have had a huge advantage in the short-term because they haven’t been sticking to the rules and other people have. That’s given them a huge advantage, so we probably couldn’t have competed with them, but we could certainly have competed with Liverpool and Arsenal and whatever else.’

“I don't think we do anything different. We always try and approach every game as best we can, given the opposition we're playing against,” McCann, pictured, told The Yorkshire Post.

“I don't think there's any real special ingredients behind it.

“It would be nice to have a home game. Since I've been here, I don't think we've had a home game in the first or second round."

Rotherham are without nine first-teamers at Bromley, with Jili Buyabu, Kian Spence and Dominic Iorfa suspended.

The Millers, who swapped divisions with Bromley in the summer, have gone 10 matches without a win. But coach Alex Bruce believes his men can take inspiration from his dad Steve's former club Manchester United, who ended a nine-match winless streak in Tuesday's Champions League.

“Confidence can be affected by a run of games,” he said. “But confidence can easily come as well.

“We've seen it, on a larger stage, with Manchester United and that result against Roma. Two-nil down at half-time, they get a last-minute winner.

“It can galvanise things. We need something similar. I've got confidence in the players.”

Bruce labeled Buyabu's red card an “act of stupidity”, but says he has calmed down after telling the Sheffield United loanee to stay away from the training ground for a few days. “It's very easy to say he can't play for the club again,” said Bruce.

“I'd be lying to you if I said I didn't feel that kind of sentiment on that Saturday night when I'm driving away after a week's prep.

“However, I am short on numbers, I've got a hell of an injury list, I haven't got the biggest of squads, I haven't got many left-sided players and I know what Jili's capable of.”

York City will be lifted by the return of two “big players” at home to Northampton Town on Saturday.

Olli Banks missed the 5-2 defeat at Grimsby Town through concussion protocols, when Hiram Boateng was suspended.

“They're two big players,” commented coach Scott Lindsey.

“It gives me more options, with the squad the way it was in the last game.”

The Minstermen are considering knee surgery for defender Morgan Williams, who suffered a grade two medial cruciate ligament injury and a meniscus tear against Barnet.

Meanwhile, Doncaster's League One game at home to Leyton Orient, scheduled for November 14, has been postponed due to international call-ups.

#1948. Luton Town vs Forest Green Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 05:05, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:20

Meeting at Kenilworth Road in the FA Cup's first round proper for the second season in a row, Luton Town and Forest Green Rovers will lock horns in a cross-division clash on Saturday.

The Hatters have progressed beyond this stage every year since 2013-14, though the Green have only lost one of their last seven matches.

Jack Wilshere's Luton are in the hunt for promotion from League One, and a strong run in the FA Cup could inspire the team in their push.

The Hatters arrive for Saturday's cup clash unbeaten in five games, winning four on the bounce prior to a 1-1 draw with Huddersfield on Tuesday.

That stalemate has Wilshere's side fourth in the third tier with 24 points after 14 matchdays, just two points behind second-placed Stockport County.

Luton's commendable campaign so far has been built on their attacking prowess, and it is notable that top-of-the-table Huddersfield are the only club to have outscored their tally of 26 goals in League One.

Saturday's hosts will be expecting to progress against their lower-tier opponents, though Wilshere is hoping for a more straightforward victory than last season's 4-3 first-round triumph over Forest Green.

The Hatters raced into a three-goal lead through Lamine Fanne and a Nahki Wells brace that day in October 2025, only to require a 92nd-minute winner from substitute Gideon Kodua after Rovers fought back to 3-3 in the second half.

Forest Green are operating without a permanent manager after Robbie Savage left the club to join Peterborough United last month, though Jonathan Gould is in charge of the National League team on a caretaker basis.

Rovers' owner Dale Vince has said that there is "No vacancy," and the club have won twice, drawn twice and lost just once with the head coach role remaining unfilled.

Most recently, Gould's side followed up their 2-0 victory over Eastleigh with a 2-2 stalemate against Harrogate Town, a particularly frustrating result given the Green held a 2-0 lead at half time.

In the FA Cup's fourth qualifying round, Forest Green were held to a 0-0 draw by Chesham, before thrashing them 5-0 in the replay, courtesy of goals from five different scorers.

The nominal caretaker boss described that attacking performance as a "Tonic," considering the team had suffered from poor finishing across their six-game winless run prior.

Looking ahead to Saturday's first round proper, it remains to be seen whether the visitors can repeat that offensive showcase against higher-tier opposition, though fans will take heart from the fact Rovers have lost on just one of their six away days this term.

Luton will be without versatile left-sided defender Kal Naismith, who was forced off after just 17 minutes against Huddersfield.

Filling the gap on Saturday, Wilshere could opt to start Harrison Ashby at right-back and shift Isiah Jones across to the left, with the duo flanking centre-backs George Johnston and Mads Andersen.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Nahki Wells may operate up top, while Kasey Palmer and Tudor Mendel-Idowu line up out wide.

As for Forest Green, they are missing striker Ricardo Rees as he recovers from the cruciate ligament injury he suffered in September.

In his absence, veteran Will Grigg could lead the line this weekend, supported by Kyle McAllister, Kyle Kelly and Bryan Ifeanyi.

Shea; Ashby, Andersen, Johnston, Jones; Walsh; Mendel-Idowu, Donley, Clark, Palmer; Wells

#1947. Arsenal sensation Max Dowman handed major new boost despite two red cards

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman has been handed his maiden call-up to the England Under-21s squad.

The Gunners sensation, 16, was on Friday named in head coach Lee Carsley’s 23-man Young Lions group for upcoming friendlies against Portugal and France.

It is the first time that Dowman will step up to U21 football at international level, having previously represented his country in the U16, U17 and U19 age categories.

He was sent off on his last appearance for the U19s in a behind-closed-doors friendly against the United States last month.

Dowman was then dismissed late on while playing for Arsenal in their shock Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood for retaliating following a heavy challenge, with the Gunners’ appeal against his ban rejected by the Football Association (FA).

That drew a visibly furious reaction from manager Mikel Arteta, who had some choice words for the teenager as he trudged off having spoken to him before the match about not reacting to any rough treatment.

Arteta was criticised in some quarters for his response to Dowman’s red card at Fleetwood, but later doubled down on his approach and insisted “we are not in Disneyland” as he warned that the player had to meet the same standards as the rest of the first-team squad.

Dowman is joined in England’s U21s squad by Arsenal team-mates Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, currently out on loan at Stevenage and Borussia Dortmund respectively, plus former Gunners youngsters Brooke Norton-Cuffy and Amario Cozier-Duberry.

Other standout selections include soaring Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni, plus Tottenham star Archie Gray, Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong and Manchester City full-back Rico Lewis, who was drafted into the senior squad last month following the injury to club team-mate Nico O’Reilly.

However, Liverpool teenager Rio Ngumoha has been promoted to the senior squad by Thomas Tuchel, while prolific Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear misses out through injury.

Following a goalless home draw with Slovakia, Carsley’s side last month qualified for the 2027 U21 European Championship, which takes place in Albania and Serbia next summer.

Their unbeaten run in qualifying was only ended by defeat to the Republic of Ireland in the final fixture, with England the current reigning back-to-back U21 champions of Europe after winning titles in both 2023 and 2025.

#1943. Michael Carrick makes bold Manchester United prediction amid Sir Alex Ferguson comparison

Michael Carrick has said that it is “possible” for Manchester United to get back to the glory years of Sir Alex Ferguson’s tenure.

The former midfielder solidified himself as a club legend under the Scot during his playing career at Old Trafford, and now he sits in the same hotseat that Ferguson left in 2013.

Carrick, meanwhile, is under serious pressure after just one win in 10 games leaves United 17th in the Premier League table, although the winless run was snapped on Tuesday with a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League.

The Red Devils have endured their worst start to a campaign in 40 years, and comparisons have been made between Carrick’s opening games of his first season in charge to Ferguson’s in 1990.

Ferguson, who was appointed United boss in 1986, was spared what had seemed to be an inevitable sacking after he beat Nottingham Forest in the FA Cup in January 1990 after a woeful start to the season that saw his side 15th in the table, with results including a 5-1 hammering by Manchester City.

Carrick has suffered the same fate this term, with many believing that he would be dismissed after the 4-1 and 3-0 defeats by Como and Bourenmouth a fortnight ago.

He was retained in-post by the club’s hierarchy ahead of the 2-0 loss at Chelsea, with it believed that the club’s hierarchy want to reassess his position during the November international break.

Ahead of another crucial Premier League tie, this time against Aston Villa, Carrick looked positively at what the future could hold for his side.

"It's difficult to bring success. It was difficult then, and it's difficult now," he said.

"It just shows you how tough it is to have sustained success, never mind moments of success.

"We've got to live in the moment. We know what we've got to do, and we've got to be focused on bringing success week to week in games.

"Then things fall into place. If you do that enough, and do it often enough, you'll bring a bigger version of it.”

The ex-England international was asked whether his current United team could be held to the same standards as that of Ferguson’s pomp, to which the head coach replied: "It's not impossible. Anything's possible.

"You've got to build. You've got to be realistic, and you've got to put things into perspective as well.

"Look at the recent history we've had, where we're trying to get to and what we want to achieve. It's not going to happen in a blink of an eye. It's not going to happen overnight.

"Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build.

"We showed a really quick response and improved a lot last season, and that shows what's possible.

"The game has certainly changed, no doubt. It always does. It evolves, and it had evolved by the time Sir Alex came in, probably after Sir Matt and the years following that.

"It evolves all the time. That's how it is. It changes, and we've got to deal with what's in front of us. That's us.

"I understand the comparisons. There's always different things to compare, but we have to live in the present as well and definitely use past experiences to help us.

"Time and patience, but we're all desperate to win football matches and win them as quickly as we possibly can."

#1942. Paris Saint-Germain vs. Troyes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 06 Nov 2026 05:24, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:57

Paris Saint-Germain enter Saturday's gameweek 10 Ligue 1 encounter at Parc des Princes seeking a seventh consecutive league victory and an 11th straight win across all competitions.

The European champions have not dropped points in two months, and Luis Enrique's men are heavy favourites to extend their dominant run against Troyes, who have claimed just one victory in their last seven matches.

PSG enter every Ligue 1 season as overwhelming title favourites, but even many of their own supporters may be surprised by their current winning sequence.

Enrique's team have largely been unremarkable during the first half of recent campaigns before surging into top form after the new year; however, they appear to have found their rhythm considerably earlier this term.

There was a sense of business as usual when PSG suffered a 2-1 defeat at Parc des Princes at the start of September, leaving Les Parisiens with just two points from their opening three matches.

They have since turned the screw, beginning with mid-September's 1-0 success over Brest before victories against Marseille, Le Mans, Strasbourg, Lyon and Le Havre propelled them to the top of the Ligue 1 table.

The Red and Blues could yet be displaced by Lille, who trail by two points, or Lyon or Paris FC, who are both three adrift, but that outcome appears unlikely.

That assessment is reinforced by Troyes' position in the top flight, with 16th-placed ESTAC just one point clear of Le Mans in the automatic relegation places.

On a positive note, Stephane Dumont's team were in the bottom two before last weekend, when Mouhamed Diop and Ismael Boura scored to secure a much-needed victory after exactly two months without one.

However, facing PSG presents an entirely different challenge, and Troyes' return of four points from six alongside consecutive clean sheets could yet prove a false dawn.

A sixth league defeat for ESTAC on Saturday could send them back into the bottom two, although that outcome depends on Le Mans defeating Monaco.

While one result appears likely, given that PSG are unbeaten in their last 10 meetings with Troyes and have won nine, Le Mans must end an eight-match winless sequence against the Monegasques.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (knee) is a long-term absentee for the capital club, while Nuno Mendes (muscle), Marquinhos (thigh) and Ousmane Dembele (thigh) are also sidelined.

Ferran Torres has outscored every teammate in Ligue 1, although the forward has now gone seven matches without scoring for Enrique's men, including four in the league.

The reigning Ligue 1 and Champions League holders were rampant in midweek, demonstrating their wealth of match-winners in a 6-0 thrashing of Villarreal; Fabian Ruiz scored twice, Desire Doue and Senny Mayulu also netted, Maghnes Akliouche registered two assists and Joao Neves contributed a goal and an assist.

ESTAC, meanwhile, have had seven different goalscorers, with Antoine Mille, Diop, Timothe Nkada, Lucas Maronnier, Jeremy Le Douaron, Ismael Boura and Renaud Ripart all finding the net.

Troyes have fewer absentees than their hosts, but Yacouba Kone (knee) will miss Saturday's match; Anis Ouzenadji (knee) is nearing a return but remains doubtful for this weekend.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:

Safonov; Zaire-Emery, Zabarnyi, Pacho, Digne; Neves, Beraldo, Ruiz; Akliouche, Torres, Godts

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz Jr, Iweru; Mille, Karim, Diop; Ifnaoui, Ripart, Nkada

Troyes have restored some confidence with four points and consecutive clean sheets, but containing the European champions represents a considerably greater challenge than their recent assignments.

Fresh from putting six past Villarreal, PSG have enough match-winners to overcome their injury absences and extend their winning sequence with a comfortable home victory.

#1941. Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur: 'Calm' Daniel Farke dismisses talk of 'difficult situation' after winless run

United's winless sequence in the league has now extended to five matches following last weekend's 2-0 reverse at Bournemouth. They have also scored just two goals along the way - ahead of Saturday lunch-time's home meeting with in-form Tottenham Hotspur.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Thursday, Leeds chief Farke admitted that he was 'struggling' in terms of offensive options.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Noah Okafor (abductor) and Anton Stach (toe) have not been involved in team training this week. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who sat out training on Thursday with a slight foot issue, was due to be back with his team-mates at Thorp Arch yesterday.

Farke believes that plenty of perspective should be applied to the winless streak.

During this period, his side produced a 'outstanding' performance at champions and league leaders Arsenal, in his view. He also felt that that Leeds should have also beaten arch-rivals Manchester United eight days later on October 18.

Farke, whose side remain unbeaten on home soil this term, said: "I don't have the feeling at all we are in a difficult situation.

"After a great start, for us it was clear that we wouldn't stay the whole season on position five or seven and it was clear there would be a period with a very difficult away game, like the one at Arsenal. I think it was an outstanding performance there.

"We had an important game against Man United and just one team should have won this game.

"Then we had two different games on the road, One good clean sheet and an away draw (at Sunderland) and against Bournemouth, let's be honest up to 30 minutes, we could have buried the game.

"If you then are there with a gift of a goal like we did, then it's difficult for us to end with points on this level against an in-form side.

"Of course no-one is happy that we didn't have this winning feeling in the last games in the dressing room. But we all could judge why this was and for that no-one is lacking confidence or is concerned.

"So, it's way more difficult if you are there with poor performances and then you lose the game and are played out of the park and you are there with back-to-back losses."

Leeds face a Spurs side who have improved of late under Roberto De Zerbi, winning their last three league fixtures.

The North London outfit also boast a strong recent record at Elland Road, having picked up three points on their previous three visits.

While Leeds last tasted victory in the league on September 14, Farke remains calm about the direction of Leeds' season.

He continued: "We are pretty clear even after our top start (in 2026-27) that for us, our aim is we want to get to 40 points as quickly as possible.

#1939. Michael Carrick replacement race takes another twist as key Manchester United figure 'set for exit'

Manchester United could lose a key member of staff who will have a big say in who replaces Michael Carrick, should the current head coach be sacked.

Carrick has come under immense scrutiny after a run of just one win in 10 games across all competitions, with that streak stretching back to late August.

The Red Devils snapped that nine-game stretch without a victory on Tuesday in a dramatic 3-2 comeback against Roma in the Champions League, which could well have saved their under-fire boss.

Many thought that Carrick would be dismissed a fortnight ago after heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth - 4-1 and 3-0 respectively - but he was kept on for the trip to Chelsea, which United lost 2-0, as Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer netted while Lisandro Martinez was sent off.

It appears that the head coach will be given until the November international break, when it has been reported that the club’s hierarchy will reassess his position, following the home Premier League game against Aston Villa on Sunday.

It is believed that there are three potential replacements that United are targeting should they decide to make a change in the dugout, with Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler all under consideration.

Nagelsmann, the former Bayern Munich and Germany boss, has an internal ally which could hand him an advantage in the race to replace Carrick.

That is Christopher Vivell, United’s director of recruitment, who the German worked with at RB Leipzig.

However, a spanner could be thrown in the works, with German outlet Bild claiming that Bayern Munich are interested in appointing Vivell.

It comes after the Bundesliga champions terminated their head of scouting Nils Schmadtke’s contract three days ago, and they have identified Vivell as an ideal replacement.

Should Vivell, who also worked for a short period at Chelsea, move back to Germany, that could come as a serious blow to Nagelsmann’s chances of landing the job at Old Trafford.
